intro: Critical care nurses handle the sickest patients, so their judgment and calm are rare strengths. The closest of the 25 careers below is Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses, with an 87% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $64,400, which means most close moves trade pay for lower stress.
why_it_works: In an ICU you watch monitors, titrate drips and react in seconds when a patient crashes. O*NET rates social perceptiveness and service orientation at 4 out of 5 for this job. BLS includes critical care nurses in the registered nurse group, so this page lists each career's median rather than a percent change. The best-paid matches are technical or academic, such as medical dosimetry.
tips: Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470 and use your precision with doses and equipment.
Try teaching through hospital education or precepting new nurses before applying to college roles.
If you want to leave the bedside but keep your license, ask about flight, transport or telehealth nursing.

faq.q: What jobs can former critical care nurses do?
faq.a: The closest matches are licensed practical nurses (87%), Paramedics (86%) and Nursing Assistants (78%), based on O*NET 31.0. Ophthalmic medical technologists are 75% matched, with a median of $50,290 for their broader group, and offer regular daytime hours.

faq.q: Which jobs for critical care nurses pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Medical Dosimetrists at $147,470, postsecondary health specialties teachers at $107,310 and Genetic Counselors at $100,040, according to BLS May 2025 data. The teaching and counseling roles usually require a graduate degree first.

faq.q: Do critical care nurses need more education to switch?
faq.a: For most paths, no. 20 of the 25 matches need no more education than critical care nurses already have, including 8 of the top 10. 5 usually need a graduate degree, and many roles in this group expect a professional certification.

faq.q: What skills should critical care nurses learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment maintenance, repairing, time management and equipment selection. Coordination already rates 3.88 out of 5 for critical care nurses in O*NET, so technical equipment skills are the main step toward dosimetry or device roles.
